title: Elvarika Ditched Managed Supabase, Saved 500MB RAM | vitalii.no
description:
Elvarika's backend ran on a managed Supabase project I didn't control the server of — the same kind of quota risk that already took down vitalii.no's own managed database once. Any migration had to go through Supabase's own tooling instead of a plain compose file I could inspect and restart myself.

I stood up a slim self-hosted Supabase stack — database, REST, auth, storage, functions and a gateway — on the same VPS behind a Cloudflare tunnel at api.elvarika.com, reusing the existing JWT secret so every anon key and logged-in session stayed valid through the cutover. A new security migration added two trigger functions that block a user from granting themselves a privileged role through the signup form, and lock the role and credits_balance columns against anyone but a privileged caller.

The managed project's dead-quota risk is gone, and dropping one piece of the old stack freed roughly 500 megabytes of RAM on a machine that has to share memory with several other services. A nightly systemd timer now backs up the database and keeps the last 14 copies.
